aesthetic-hypertrophy.name: Aesthetic Engine: 5-Day Hypertrophy
aesthetic-hypertrophy.description: For experienced lifters who enjoy five gym days. Balanced upper/lower muscle building with extra shoulder work. Full gym; roughly 55–75 minutes per session.
guidelines: Train Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday. Keep Wednesday and Sunday free for recovery; add time between sessions if recovery suffers.
The listed sets are working sets. Warm up first, then use progressively heavier practice sets before your first heavy lifts.
Finish most sets with about 2 good repetitions left. Keep the same controlled range of motion; failure is not required.
When every set reaches the top of its rep range with clean form, increase by the smallest available weight next time and return to the lower end. Otherwise keep the weight and build reps.
Keep the plan for 6–8 weeks before judging progress. If fatigue accumulates or performance drops across several sessions, use fewer sets and lighter loads for a week. Do not train through pain.

classic-ppl.description: For experienced lifters who can consistently recover from six gym days. Two push, pull and leg sessions with distinct emphases. Full gym; about 45–65 minutes.
guidelines: Sunday is rest. Choose the 4-day Upper/Lower plan if six days is hard to sustain. Pull days use supported rows, leaving heavy hip hinges to leg days.

full-body-classic.name: Classic Foundation: 3-Day Full Body
full-body-classic.description: A manageable starting point for beginners and returning lifters. Repeat key movement patterns instead of learning a new routine every day. Gym with dumbbells, bench, leg press and cables; about 40–55 minutes.
guidelines: Use non-consecutive days. For the first two weeks, leave 3–4 good repetitions in reserve and prioritize learning the setup over adding weight. Ask for help with unfamiliar equipment.

home-forge-dumbbells.name: Home Forge: 4-Day Dumbbells
home-forge-dumbbells.description: Upper/lower training with adjustable dumbbells and an adjustable bench; no cables, barbell or pull-up station. For lifters comfortable with the basics. About 40–60 minutes.
guidelines: Train Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday. Use a stable low platform for the front-foot-elevated split squat. If your dumbbells become too light, use the top of the rep range with controlled form; do not invent extra weight in the log.

athletic-performance.name: Athletic Engine: 3-Day Strength & Power
athletic-performance.description: General strength and low-rep power practice for experienced lifters, not a sport-specific conditioning plan. Full gym with trap bar, kettlebell and low platform; about 50–65 minutes.
guidelines: Train on non-consecutive days and account for your sport sessions. Learn swings and push presses before using this plan. Use light-to-moderate loads on these two lifts and stop the set as soon as speed or technique drops, even before the target reps.
Do not apply automatic rep-range progression to swings or push presses: add load only while every repetition stays fast and controlled. This plan does not replace aerobic training or sport practice.

machine-foundation.name: Machine Foundation: 3-Day Full Body
machine-foundation.description: For beginners, returning lifters or anyone who prefers machine setups to free weights. Three repeatable full-body sessions using selectorized/sled machines and cables. About 40–55 minutes; check that your gym has the listed machines.
guidelines: Use non-consecutive days. Set the seat, pads and range of motion before loading; record the same machine’s load each time, since stack numbers differ between machines. Leave 3–4 repetitions in reserve while learning.
